goal: The rope: do what the NEXT line asks until dusk, then walk the path from the village to the ghat, light the lamp (F) and look steadily at each snake until it turns out to be a rope; then sleep at home (E at the indigo door) and, in the morning, try V. Answer the questions at the end.

findings.title: NEXT at the snakes is cut at the right edge at 640x360 ('(1 of 3' / '(2')
findings.detail: The count after 'look at it steadily' runs off the window. Seen in the previous runs too.
findings.repro: at dusk, turn one snake to rope and read NEXT

findings.title: Snakes are hard to find from the bearing alone; a low kerb on the path blocks the straight line
findings.detail: Looking for the third snake, NEXT said '7 m to your left' and then '6 m to your left' after I turned left and walked, because a low wall by the river stopped me without a sign. Hiding the HUD (H) was the quickest way to spot the coil.
findings.repro: after two ropes, follow the bearing to the third snake

findings.title: The waking message runs off the bottom after V
findings.detail: '... Live the day as it comes, or step back' is cut at the bottom edge at 640x360.
findings.repro: sleep after both teachings, wait to the morning, press V

verdict: Unlike the previous run's s03, which stopped inside the dream, this session slept through: the dream and deep sleep both say they pass by themselves, and waking on 22 March and V worked. The rope chapter works; finding each snake still leans on the bearing and on hiding the HUD. secondsToObjective are wall-clock seconds from pt start (no probe); this session was driven by the proctor, interleaved with another session, on a shared machine, so the times are long. The proctor had read the #39 diff, so this is not a naive first-time read.

answers.question: In your own words, what did you think the game was about? What did the rope and the snake, and the clay and the pots, mean?
answers.answer: The named pots are one clay: the names and shapes are real as uses but the stuff is one, and breaking a pot loses nothing of the clay. The snake on the path was a rope all along; fear came from not seeing in poor light and ended when I held the lamp and looked steadily. Sleep extends it: waking, dream and deep sleep came and went, and the waking text says you were there for all three.

answers.question: Did anything feel preachy, confusing, or inaccurate (in the teaching, the verses in the codex, or how the tradition is described)? Say what and where; if nothing did, say so.
answers.answer: Nothing felt preachy: the game shows, and the codex quotes its sources with Sanskrit and a named translation. 'Other schools' gives Visistadvaita and Dvaita fair, short readings and says the game follows one school. The sleep no longer confused me. I cannot judge the translations, some of which are marked as working translations awaiting review.
